1.	Moderate distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis with interstitial tearing involving approximately 15% of the cross-sectional area of the superficial tendon fibers.
2.	Mild proximal patellar tendinosis with low-grade interstitial tearing.
3.	Findings suggestive of active patellofemoral maltracking.
4.	Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

In keeping with the provided history there is a bucket-handle tear of the lateral meniscus. The body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus are diminutive and there is a large flipped fragment demonstrated within the intercondylar notch passing anterior to the posterior cruciate ligament. Linear signal also extends into the anterior horn of lateral meniscus consistent with extension of the tear to the anterior horn.

There is an associated osteochondral injury seen to the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. In this region there is mild contour flattening of the articular surface of the posterior aspect of lateral femoral condyle associated with regions of focal cartilage fraying and articular cartilage loss. There is edema seen within the lateral femoral condyle in association with this finding in keeping with resolving bone contusion. Small marginal osteophytes are seen to the lateral joint compartment consistent with early osteoarthritic change.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained. Minimal degenerative spurring is seen at the articular surfaces of the patellofemoral joint. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits measuring about 8 mm.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact and unremarkable.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact and unremarkable.

The medial collateral ligament is intact and unremarkable.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, the fibular collateral ligament, the biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small Baker's cyst. There is stranding seen within the fascial constraints of the medial head of the gastrocnemius in continuity with the Baker's cyst in keeping with a ruptured Baker's cyst. There is associated mild fluid around the pes anserine tendons which may correlate clinically with mild pes anserine bursitis.

There is a small knee effusion demonstrated with reactive synovitis. There is low signal stranding in Hoffa's fat.

Marrow signal is otherwise within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Complex bucket-handle tear of the lateral meniscus as described.

Associated with the lateral meniscal tear there is an osteochondral impaction injury of the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle as described. Marrow edema remains in the lateral femoral condyle in keeping with resolving bone contusion.

Evidence of ruptured Baker's cyst.

Possible mild pes anserine bursitis.

Additional findings as noted.
